label: thm:ami
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Compositionality implies algorithmic mutual information

title: Proof
body_md:
The two parts can always be compressed independently by concatenating their model descriptions and residual codes. Because \(m_x\) is an optimal model of the whole, we have that:
\begin{align}
    K(m_x)+l_{m_x}(x)
    \leq
    K(m_{x_a})+l_{m_{x_a}}(x_a)
    +
    K(m_{x_b})+l_{m_{x_b}}(x_b) .
\end{align}
If \(C(x_a,x_b\to x)>0\), the no-tie assumption in \cref{eq:no_neutral_ties} makes this inequality strict. Therefore:
\begin{align}
    K(x)
    &=
    K(m_x)+l_{m_x}(x) \\
    &<
    K(m_{x_a})+l_{m_{x_a}}(x_a)
    +
    K(m_{x_b})+l_{m_{x_b}}(x_b) \\
    &=
    K(x_a)+K(x_b) .
\end{align}
Hence:
\begin{align}
    I(x_a:x_b)
    =
    K(x_a)+K(x_b)-K(x)
    >
    0 .
\end{align}

For the reverse direction, consider a case in which the same model \(m\) is the Occam's razor model of \(x_a\), \(x_b\), and \(x\), and write \(c=K(m)>0\). The whole can reuse this model description:
\begin{align}
    K(x)
    &\leq
    c+l_m(x_a)+l_m(x_b) \\
    &<
    2c+l_m(x_a)+l_m(x_b) \\
    &=
    K(x_a)+K(x_b) .
\end{align}
Thus \(I(x_a:x_b)>0\). Nevertheless, we have that:
\begin{align}
    C(x_a,x_b\to x)
    =
    K(m\mid m,m)
    =
    0 .
\end{align}
Therefore, positive algorithmic mutual information does not imply novel compositional structure.

label: thm:total_compositionality
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:total_compositionality}
Let $T$ be a finite rooted, ordered decomposition tree for $x$,
and suppose that the Occam's razor model $m_{x_v}$ is
well-defined at every node $v$. Let $\tau_T$ denote the
unlabeled ordered tree shape, and let
$M_{\mathrm{leaf}} := (m_{x_\ell})_{\ell\in\mathrm{Leaves}(T)}$
list the leaf models in left-to-right order. Then:
\begin{align}
    S_T(x)
    \geq K(m_x) - K(\tau_T,M_{\mathrm{leaf}}) - O(1),
\end{align}
where the constant is independent of $x$ and $T$.
head: environment
name: Model complexity bounds total compositionality

title: Proof
body_md:
For each internal node $v$ with ordered children
$v_1,\ldots,v_{k_v}$, choose a shortest prefix program $p_v$
that outputs $m_{x_v}$ given
$(m_{x_{v_1}},\ldots,m_{x_{v_{k_v}}})$. By definition,
\begin{align}
    |p_v|
    = K(m_{x_v}\mid m_{x_{v_1}},\ldots,m_{x_{v_{k_v}}})
    = C_{T,x}(v).
\end{align}
Construct a description consisting of a shortest prefix
program for $(\tau_T,M_{\mathrm{leaf}})$, followed by the
programs $p_v$ in postorder, so that children precede
their parents.

A fixed decoder first recovers the tree shape and leaf
models. It then processes the internal nodes in postorder,
running each $p_v$ with the already reconstructed child
models as its auxiliary input. Since the programs are
prefix-free and the tree determines their number and
order, no additional delimiters are required. At the
root, the decoder outputs $m_x$. Consequently,
\begin{align}
    K(m_x)
    &\leq K(\tau_T,M_{\mathrm{leaf}})
       + \sum_{v\in\mathrm{Int}(T)} |p_v| + O(1) \\
    &= K(\tau_T,M_{\mathrm{leaf}}) + S_T(x) + O(1).
\end{align}
Rearranging proves the result.

label: cor:fully_refined_maximum
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:fully_refined_maximum}
Let $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, with $n\geq 1$. Consider all rooted,
ordered decomposition trees of $x$ whose internal nodes
have at least two children and whose nodes represent
nonempty substrings. There exists a tree maximizing
$S_T(x)$ whose leaves are individual bits.
head: environment
name: Maximal decompositions can be fully refined

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\ell$ be a leaf of a decomposition tree $T$, and
let $R$ be a decomposition tree of $x_\ell$. Replacing
$\ell$ by $R$ produces a refinement $T'$ satisfying
\begin{align}
    S_{T'}(x) = S_T(x) + S_R(x_\ell) \geq S_T(x).
\end{align}
Indeed, every existing internal node retains the same
substring and immediate child substrings, so its score
is unchanged, while all newly introduced scores are
nonnegative.

There are finitely many admissible decomposition trees,
so a maximizer exists. Starting from any maximizer,
recursively split each leaf of length greater than one.
The resulting tree has individual bits as leaves and
cannot have a smaller score. Since the original tree
was maximal, the refined tree is also maximal.
head: environment

label: cor:maximal_compositionality_bound
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Maximal compositionality bounds model complexity

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $B_n$ be the binary decomposition obtained by
recursively splitting each substring into two parts
whose lengths differ by at most one, stopping at
individual bits. Its ordered tree shape is computable
from $n$, and its leaf-model tuple consists of $n$
copies of the fixed model $m_{\varnothing}$. Hence
\begin{align}
    K(\tau_{B_n},M_{\mathrm{leaf}})
    \leq K(n)+O(1).
\end{align}
Applying \cref{thm:total_compositionality} gives
\begin{align}
    S_{B_n}(x) \geq K(m_x)-K(n)-O(1).
\end{align}
Finally, maximality implies
$S_{T_x^{\mathrm{max}}}(x)\geq S_{B_n}(x)$,
which proves the claim.

label: cor:minimal_complete
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Minimal complete decompositions

title: Proof
body_md:
The only internal node of $T_\star$ is its root, so
\begin{align}
    S_{T_\star}(x)
    =K\bigl(m_x\mid
      \underbrace{m_{\varnothing},\ldots,m_{\varnothing}}
                  _{n\text{ copies}}\bigr)
    =K(m_x\mid n)+O(1).
\end{align}
The final equality holds because the tuple determines
$n$, and conversely $n$ determines the tuple using the
fixed model $m_{\varnothing}$. This proves the upper bound.

For the lower bound, every complete tree has $n$ leaves
and at most $n-1$ internal nodes. Its ordered shape can
therefore be encoded in $O(n)$ bits. Since all leaf
models equal $m_{\varnothing}$, the shape also determines
their tuple, giving
\begin{align}
    K(\tau_T,M_{\mathrm{leaf}})=O(n).
\end{align}
By \cref{thm:total_compositionality}, uniformly over
complete trees,
\begin{align}
    S_T(x)\geq K(m_x)-O(n).
\end{align}
Taking the minimum proves the stated bounds. Suppressing
the indicated coding terms yields the idealized equality.
head: environment

label: cor:minimal_unrestricted
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Minimal unrestricted decompositions

title: Proof
body_md:
The root-only tree has no internal nodes, so its score
is an empty sum and equals zero. Every decomposition
score is a sum of nonnegative conditional complexities
and is therefore nonnegative.

label: thm:recursive_consistency
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Recursive consistency of maximal decompositions

title: Proof
body_md:
Each set $\mathcal{T}(y)$ is finite and nonempty, so its maximum exists. Fix a node $v$ of $T$ and any $R\in\mathcal{T}(x_v)$. Replace $T_v$ by $R$, identifying the root of $R$ with $v$, and denote the resulting tree by $T'$. This is an admissible decomposition of $x$.

Every internal node outside the replaced subtree retains the same substring and the same ordered list of immediate child substrings. In particular, the parent of $v$, if present, still has $x_v$ as the same child substring. Since each model depends only on its substring, all local scores outside the replaced subtree remain unchanged. Consequently,
\begin{align}
    S_{T'}(x)
    = S_T(x) - S_{T_v}(x_v) + S_R(x_v).
\end{align}
Maximality of $T$ implies $S_{T'}(x)\leq S_T(x)$, and hence $S_R(x_v)\leq S_{T_v}(x_v)$. Since $R$ was arbitrary, $T_v$ is a maximizing decomposition of $x_v$. If $R$ is also maximizing, the displayed identity gives $S_{T'}(x)=S_T(x)$, proving the final claim.
